settings.label: Public IP endpoint
settings.description: Fetched with a 3 s timeout and kept 10 minutes; JSON with `ip` (and `city`, `country`, `org` when it has them) or a bare address. Empty: no public IP row.

settings.label: Known networks
settings.description: One line per network, `SSID = kind label:Name icon:X`, keyed on the SSID or on the gateway (`192.168.1.1 = ...` also covers a cable into the same router and a Wi-Fi name macOS declines to reveal). Every field is optional and the order is free: a bare word is the kind, `label:` renames the network on the bar (the palette keeps the real SSID; a name with a space goes in quotes, `label:"Cafe Corner"`), `icon:` is one emoji or a Nerd Font glyph pasted in (the Icons palette copies one) drawn instead of the signal, hotspot, open or wired mark. Keyed fields rather than positions so a line with only an icon needs no placeholders. Kinds: `hide` drops the bar item entirely, since the network you are on almost all the time can tell you nothing and its absence is the point; `hotspot` marks one that costs data; `public` one to distrust. For example `192.168.1.1 = hide icon:󰋜`, `Cafe Wifi = hotspot label:Cafe icon:☕`.

store.tagline: Every IP this machine has right now, Enter copies it
features: This machine: each interface's IPv4 and global IPv6 (`en0 · Wi-Fi`, `eth0`), the Tailscale IPv4 and IPv6, the hostname and the Bonjour `.local` name
Internet: the public IP with the city, country and organisation the endpoint gives, fetched once and kept ten minutes
Network: the default gateway with its interface, the DNS servers in resolver order
The value is the row's name, so it reads at a glance; `enter` copies it, `cmd+enter` opens the Network settings
Opens with the detail pane: interface, kind, SSID, security, signal, MAC and status for an address; city, region and organisation for the public IP
Live: listed again when the panel shows and the last listing is over a minute old; `cmd+r` fetches the public IP again

actions.title: Open Network settings
actions.description: System Settings on macOS; gnome-control-center, systemsettings or nm-connection-editor on Linux.

network.description: Live rows, listed again when the panel shows and the last listing is over a minute old; ⌘R lists now and fetches the public IP again.

status.title: Network status
status.description: The active network, as its name (or the label Known networks gives it), or with Icon only as a glyph alone: signal strength on Wi-Fi, its own mark for a hotspot or an open network, wired, or offline, or the icon Known networks gives that network (home, office, cafe, phone). A network set to `hide` there draws nothing. Click opens Network Settings; the popover names the connection and its kind, then the interface, the address, the gateway, the signal and security, and the DNS servers.
